title: App shell
description: The frame of a multi-page app: a floating bento sidebar (w-52, collapses to a w-14 icon rail) on bg-canvas, the content panel beside it, and MobileTabBar at the bottom on phones. Items can carry sub-items that open only while their parent is chosen. This docs site is an AppShell.
when: Every app with several pages (dashboards, admin, store back office).
An area with its own sub-views that people switch between often (mailbox folders, saved views): sub-items under one nav item.

instead.need: A single-screen tool or editor (3D, canvas)
2–4 sibling views of one page that do not need a place in the menu

a11y: The sidebar is a nav landmark; the active item has aria-current; the collapse state is remembered per app (storageKey).
An item with sub-items has aria-expanded; its sub-items are a list named after it, the active one with aria-current.
notes: Render it once in the root layout (or a route group layout); pages render only their content.
Page items take an href: they stay next/link links even when onSelect is set (onSelect then only reports the click). Never route with onSelect + router.push (shell-nav-href).

Never gate the shell behind a page skeleton (shell-gate): a route loading.tsx next to the layout shimmers the content only, and the boot / session check before the layout is known renders BootLoader once in the layout. A page never renders AppShell or imports a component that does (app-shell-in-page).
MobileTabBar is used by AppShell; render it yourself only in a custom shell.
Sub-items (children) are closed by default: they open under their parent while the parent or one of them is the activeId, and close when another item is chosen. One level only.
Sub-items take an optional grey icon (give every sub-item of a parent one, or none); no colour dot or count (the menu stays neutral, §4). Put counts and colours in the page.
The rail (w-14), widths below lg and phones never show sub-items: read useAppShell().submenuVisible and give the page its own picker (a CustomSelect in the toolbar) when it is false.
Choosing the parent alone usually opens its first sub-item: map it in onSelect.
